clue.text: Really brief speaker shows it

definitions.note: noun sense: 'it' is short for Italian, the sweet red drink in a gin and it

indicators.note: brief tells us to cut the word short, losing its final letter

parts.note: really means very
the mouth is the organ we speak with

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped talker gives something away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' looks like a pronoun but is the definition: in 'gin and it', it stands for Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword convention from the bar order gin and it, where it is Italian fortified wine.

clue.text: I don't know what a poor student gets

definitions.meaning: said when declining to answer a quiz question
the lowest successful exam grade, just scraping through

explanation.surface: A mediocre student's shrug and the grade it earns.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiz contestant declines a question with this word; a weak student scrapes this exam result.

clue.text: Two boys one persecuted

parts.note: the first of the two boys, Vic, short for Victor
the second of the two boys, Tim, short for Timothy

explanation.surface: Two lads pick on a third.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two boys' supplies two short boys' names placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone harmed or bullied by others is a sufferer, a target of abuse.

clue.text: Bachelor, defended by two friends with energy, is possibly touched

indicators.note: the bachelor is protected on both sides, so it sits within the pair of friends

parts.note: a friend is a pal, so two of them
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A single man flanked by two mates and full of energy may be a bit mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touched' looks like 'slightly crazy', but means physically felt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tangible can be felt by hand, so it may be touched.

clue.text: University course taken up by Poles with no accent

parts.note: N and S, the north and south poles

indicators.note: in a down entry, taking up means reading upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a meal course: pudding

explanation.surface: A student's course is chosen by Polish classmates who speak without accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns DESSERT to TRESSED; 'by' simply puts the Poles beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllable without stress carries no emphasis, i.e. no accent.

clue.text: Talk with one criminal shedding ball and chain

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: shedding says a letter is dropped from the word one

parts.note: taken as written before losing a letter
O, a round shape like a ball

explanation.surface: A convict talks after shaking off the ball and chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' shedding O leaves NE; 'criminal' rearranges TALK plus NE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental band worn round the ankle is often a fine jewellery chain.

clue.text: Drug case follows that of suicide

indicators.note: the grammatical case comes after the casing letters
the case of suicide, read as its outer letters, its casing

parts.note: the dative is a grammatical case

explanation.surface: A drug case comes after a suspected suicide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' works twice: the grammatical DATIVE, and 'that of suicide' meaning the word's casing, S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A calming medicine that sedates is a drug given to relax a patient.

clue.text: Cover of Elton composer put in bars

indicators.note: the cover of a word is its outside letters

parts.note: John Cage, the American avant-garde composer

explanation.surface: A cover version of an Elton John song by another composer lands in the music bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' looks musical but means a cage's bars.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut an animal behind bars is to confine it in a cage.

clue.text: Crawling fellow leaves cover outdoors

indicators.note: the fellow departs from the word, removing his letter

parts.note: fawning means toadying, crawling

explanation.surface: A grovelling man drops leaves on the patio cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like foliage, fitting 'outdoors', but is the verb of departing.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas sheet fixed over a shop window or patio shelters people outside.

clue.text: Intoxicating drink from the right prophet

indicators.note: reading from the right means reading backwards in an across entry

parts.note: soma, the ritual drink of Vedic India

explanation.surface: A prophet's intoxicating drink comes from the righteous.
explanation.definitionFit: An Old Testament minor prophet has a biblical book named after him.

clue.text: Time round Great Lake as the final thing

parts.note: O is round in shape
capital as an old-fashioned exclamation meaning excellent

explanation.surface: A trip round one of the Great Lakes is the last thing on an itinerary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great Lake' looks like a single proper name but splits into CAPITAL and L.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means as a climax or crowning touch, often of a run of mishaps.

clue.text: Rolling around in mud's a revealing practice

indicators.note: rolling about mixes the letters up

explanation.surface: Wallowing in mud is a habit that exposes a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Going naked exposes everything, so the habit is literally revealing.

clue.text: Check setter's trapped, without a little money

parts.note: the setter says I'm, i.e. I am

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the trapped word goes round the coin

parts.note: pent means confined, shut in
a dime is a ten-cent coin

explanation.surface: The setter is caught short with no small change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old sense 'outside', so the trapped word wraps the coin. A dime is a US ten-cent piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle that hinders progress acts as a check or restraint.

clue.text: Spooner's wonderful company for social chats

indicators.note: the Rev. Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: fab, slang for fabulous
guests are company you entertain

explanation.surface: A lovely set of visitors makes for good talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The swap is by sound: GUESTS is said 'gests', so its G and FAB's F trade places.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal gatherings for long, gossipy talk; gab is idle chatter.

clue.text: Bubbly's cold, getting cooler

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
hipper means more fashionable, cooler

explanation.surface: Champagne is cold and getting colder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbly' looks like champagne, fitting 'cold', but means lively.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheerful, lively person can be called bubbly or perky.

clue.text: Erstwhile show-off lowering level of European publicity

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: in a down entry, lowering the letter moves it further down the word

parts.note: a poseur is a show-off

explanation.surface: A former poser loses status in the European media.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lowering level of European' moves the E of POSEUR down one place, giving POSURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Media coverage that puts someone in the public eye gives them exposure.

clue.text: Compiler of heavenly catalogue that's less orderly

definitions.meaning: Charles ..., the French astronomer whose list of nebulae and clusters is still used

explanation.surface: An astronomer's star list is untidier than it should be.
explanation.walkthrough: The astronomer's name is said 'messy-ay' but spelt like 'more untidy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Messier catalogued deep-sky objects; the same spelling is the comparative of untidy.

clue.text: Appealing sort of dash, like a 25

parts.note: an en dash, the punctuation mark
the entry at 25 can mean a feasible contender, i.e. workable

explanation.surface: A dashing athlete looks attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dash' looks like running, tying to 25, but is the en dash in typography.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worth envying is desirable, hence appealing.

clue.text: Navratilova triumphantly covering court

indicators.note: the two words cover, conceal, the letters inside them

explanation.surface: Martina Navratilova dominates the tennis court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a tennis court but means a courtyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtyard or open central hall in a building is a court.

clue.text: Person sitting on bench drank around warehouse

parts.note: a substitute waits on the bench in team sports

indicators.note: around turns the word the other way

parts.note: toped means drank heavily

explanation.surface: A substitute on the bench had a drink at the warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A subsidiary depot is a storage place, a lesser warehouse.

clue.text: Finished milk dish that's on the turn

parts.note: to milk is to exploit, use

indicators.note: turning the word over reverses it

parts.note: pud, British slang for pudding

explanation.surface: A milk pudding that has gone sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'milk' and 'on the turn' suggest souring milk; milk is the verb 'exploit'. PUD is British slang for pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplies that are consumed entirely are exhausted, all gone.

clue.text: Leaves to eat in French bar of ill-repute

parts.note: en is French for in
a dive is a seedy bar

explanation.surface: Salad served in a French dive bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter salad plant, its leaves eaten raw.

clue.text: One may take flight the day before clash

parts.note: the eve is the day before an event
to jar is to clash, conflict

explanation.surface: Someone flees on the eve of a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialect name for the nightjar, a bird, so it may take flight.

clue.text: A letter for free

parts.note: per, as in 'a day' meaning per day
a missive is a letter

explanation.surface: A letter going for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' means 'each', as in 'ten pounds a head'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient and liberal, allowing freedom of behaviour.

clue.text: People of intelligence love to have the last word

parts.note: the CIA, the US Central Intelligence Agency
O, love meaning nil in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Spies who love having the final say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People of intelligence' suggests clever folk; it is the spy agency.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian farewell, the word spoken on parting.

clue.text: Young animal on earth possibly eight

parts.note: a cub is a young fox, lion or bear

explanation.surface: A cub on the ground might be one of eight in a litter.
explanation.walkthrough: Eight is two times two times two.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight is a third power, an example of such a number.

clue.text: Dashing fellow who's caught up in traffic

definitions.meaning: one who dashes, i.e. a sprinter
a smuggler, as in a drug or gun trafficker

explanation.surface: A dashing man is stuck in a jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' looks like cars but means illegal trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinter dashes; a smuggler is a gun or drug carrier.

clue.text: This person attending dance is a bit of a dish

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me
at, as in at a party
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: The setter at a dance is rather attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of a dish' looks like 'rather attractive' but is literally part of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball of minced meat is one item of a meal, so a piece of a dish.
